title: Your Apple Watch can now turn hallway chats into meeting summaries and action items
excerpt: Start recording with one tap on Apple Watch and sync searchable transcripts, summaries, and tasks across devices.
content_html:
Published Oct 28, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT

Sara Heritage is a tech and gaming journalist, who's currently making her way up to Master Ball rank in Pokemon Champions. Bylines in IGN, GAMINGbible, The Gamer and more. You can usually find her tinkering with tech, or restoring old consoles, always with one of her 3 cats nearby. Come and talk with her over on Twitter @SHeritageJourno.

Summary

  • Flowtica expands to Apple Watch, Mac, and web to capture and transcribe meetings across devices.
  • Apple Watch app records spontaneous chats with one-tap, marks highlights, and uploads offline captures.
  • Summaries, searchable transcripts, and action items centralize notes; apps free to download, use plan minutes.

Flowtica, a popular AI productivity app, is expanding its meeting productivity software platform to Apple Watch, Mac, and web browsers. Now you can capture conversations and online meetings, generate searchable transcripts, summaries, and action items, and access your meeting information through Flowtica's connected AI ecosystem.

For example, after a team meeting, Flowtica can automatically deliver a summary and action items to all attendees, saving you the manual effort of note-taking and follow-up emails. Salespeople can quickly share highlights from a customer call with their colleagues, and project managers can track decisions and assign tasks with less hassle. These features help you save time, keep everyone on the same page, and make it easier to stay organized across your projects.

Flowtica's latest hardware rollout could save you hours in admin meetings

I'll definitely be using this the next time a meeting could've been an email

Traditionally, AI-powered meeting assistants have been bound to desktop apps, specific video-conferencing software integrations like Zoom or Teams, or smartphone apps that require you to pull your phone out and tap around while someone is talking. The move aims to make it easier for professionals to record, transcribe, and organize both in-person and online meetings across multiple devices.

I’m particularly interested in how the Apple Watch app can help you transcribe and capture spontaneous conversations, from impromptu client discussions and hallway exchanges to ideas shared between meetings. You can start recording with one tap from a watch-face complication, Smart Stack or Control Center on supported devices, and mark important moments with FlowMark, including via Double Tap on compatible Apple Watch models. Recordings can be captured offline and uploaded when connectivity returns, with transcription, summaries, action items and review available through the Flowtica app on the paired iPhone. Some of my best ideas come from pints in the pub, so I’ll finally be able to leave my notes app of half-finished ideas behind.

Recordings and meeting notes come together in one Flowtica library, so no matter where you are, your information can be captured and centralized.

Flowtica's expanded software platform complements its existing hardware portfolio, including Scribe, its AI-powered recording pen, and Verso, its MagSafe-compatible AI recording device with an integrated e-paper display.

While Apple Watch supports spontaneous conversations and Mac and Web address online meeting workflows, Scribe and Verso offer purpose-built solutions for longer or more demanding in-person recording environments.

All three applications launch October 28. Flowtica for Apple Watch will be available through the Flowtica iOS app, Flowtica for Mac will be offered as a direct download at flowtica.ai, and Flowtica Web will be accessible at web.flowtica.ai. All three are free to download or access, with AI processing minutes drawn from users’ existing Flowtica plans.
